<p class="paper-authors"><span class="paper-author">Sobhan Badakhshan</span>, <span class="paper-author">Soroush Senemmar</span>, <span class="paper-author me">Honglin Li</span>, <span class="paper-author">Jie Zhang</span></p>
<p class="paper-venue"><em>2022 IEEE Kansas Power and Energy Conference (KPEC)</em>, pp. 1–6, 2022.</p>
<section aria-labelledby="abstract"><h2 id="abstract">Abstract</h2>
<p class="paper-abstract">The transition to low-carbon electrical grids has enabled a rapid growth in offshore wind energy. In the meantime, producing green hydrogen from offshore wind farms has also gained wide attention in recent years. Among many challenges, energy transferring from offshore wind farms (especially for those in deep water) to the shoreline infrastructure has been explored in various ways. In this paper, unmanned surface hydrogen ships are explored as mobile energy resources to replace hydrogen pipelines to transfer hydrogen generated from offshore wind farms in deep water, in conjunction with unmanned battery ships for electricity transmission. The hydrogen/battery ships could charge from offshore wind farms and discharge their energy when plugged-in to the terrestrial grid or onshore hydrogen infrastructure. The schedules of the ships are optimized based on the offshore wind farm generation, weather conditions, and ship sailing timing. Results showed that by combining the hydrogen ship, battery ship, and onsite hydrogen storage tanks, more than 99% of the offshore wind farm generation could be successfully transmitted to the shore side infrastructure.</p>
<p class="paper-source">Abstract source: <a href="https://henryutd2021.github.io/files/papers/badakhshan2022integrating.pdf">PDF page 1</a>.</p></section>
